goals: Mechanistic: explain how ELM partitions precipitation into ET, surface runoff, and sub-surface drainage across the Naches basin's elevation and soil heterogeneity
Validation: NONE possible in-domain — observations_available is empty; recorded as a gap

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM resolves 1-D water partitioning; spatial sampling spans the basin's heterogeneity. No lateral process is required for a partitioning study.

answerable: Soil-texture control on ET/runoff/drainage partitioning (SSURGO is a per-column lever)

Elevation/climate control PARTIALLY — NLDAS-2 (12 km) resolves orographic precip/temperature gradients across this 1625 m-relief basin, so elevation-stratified columns carry a real climate signal, not pure soil confound
Snowmelt-driven partitioning timing (SWE/H2OSNO/QSNOMELT are in default output)

not_answerable.aspect: Fine-scale (sub-12 km) elevation and rain-snow-transition partitioning, and ridgetop peak-SWE magnitude
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 has no within-cell lapse rate; 12 km cells average over terrain and underestimate ridgetop SWE

not_answerable.aspect: Any observational validation of partitioning in-domain
not_answerable.why: observations_available is empty for this HUC
not_answerable.needs: observation-dataset ingest (SNOTEL SWE, flux ET, streamflow) for HUC 17030002

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation band × dominant soil class), oversampled at the rain-snow transition
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands × 2 dominant soil classes = 6 base strata (6 columns); +1 replicate per stratum to gauge within-stratum spread where a second dominant soil exists (up to +4); +4 extra concentrated in the mid-elevation rain-snow transition where melt timing and soil-moisture/drainage exchange are most sensitive. Totals 14 — spans the drivers without a blind 20-point grid.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate in the mid-elevation rain-snow transition band (steepest melt-timing/partitioning gradient) and oversample valley bottoms/riparian corridors where drainage and soil-moisture storage dominate; upper band sampled for snow-dominated partitioning (with ridgetop-SWE caveat).
sampling_strategy.replication: One light replicate per elevation band on the alternate dominant soil, to separate soil signal from elevation signal within a band.

sampling_plan.reason: Low-elevation warm/rain-dominated end-member on high-infiltration soil — isolates infiltration/drainage-dominated partitioning.
Same climate band on low-infiltration soil — isolates soil-texture control on runoff vs drainage at low elevation.
Steepest melt-timing gradient on high-infiltration soil — the most partitioning-sensitive stratum, oversampled.
Rain-snow transition on low-infiltration soil — tests runoff generation under mixed rain/snow inputs, oversampled.
Snowmelt-dominated partitioning on high-infiltration soil (ridgetop SWE underestimated — flagged).
Snowmelt-dominated partitioning on low-infiltration soil — snow input × low drainage capacity end-member.

validation_design.comparison: none — no co-located data; would require analog-site or external ingest

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 baseline forcing, native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start

requires_capabilities.why: NLDAS-2 at 12 km cannot resolve within-cell terrain or ridgetop snow
requires_capabilities.blocks: fine-scale rain-snow-transition and ridgetop peak-SWE partitioning

drainage/recharge and water table are slow states; cold-start at 8.8 m default gives initialization artifacts

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM + SSURGO raster sampling and HUC boundary resolver
requires_capabilities.why: downstream expander must convert these placement rules into concrete points

assumptions: User's demand for 20 coordinates + full configs is out of scope for design mode; coordinates/configs are produced downstream — strategy provided instead.
Naches is CONUS, so NLDAS-2 (elevation-resolving) forcing applies rather than Qian T62.
Two dominant soil classes adequately span SSURGO texture per elevation band; the expander confirms actual dominant classes.
Study targets long-term partitioning, so multi-year forcing within 1980-2018 plus warm start is used; runoff routing to a gage is not required.
open_questions: Are SNOTEL or streamflow records actually available for this HUC that could be ingested to enable validation?
Which forcing period/water years should define the partitioning climatology (full 1980-2018 vs a representative subset given ~30 min/simulated-year/column cost)?
Is any streamflow-aggregation/routing step desired, or is per-column partitioning sufficient?
